one_liner: Research FP16 FFT kernels that run radix-16 butterflies on NVIDIA tensor cores; beats cuFFT half precision on V100/A100.
what_it_does: Computes forward, unnormalized, in-place complex-to-complex FP16 FFTs in batches, 1D (a fixed table of power-of-two sizes: 256, 512, 1024, 2^17-2^19 and 2^24-2^27) and 2D (Nx in {256, 512}, Ny in {256, 512, 1024}). The API is two C functions, tcfftCreate(&plan, n, batch) and tcfftExec(plan, half* data), with a separate header and plan struct for 2D; there is no destroy, inverse, real-input or strided-layout call. The caller must hand it input already in digit-reversed order (the gen_rev permutation lives in the test harness, not the library), so it is not a drop-in for cufftXtExec.
how_it_is_fast: Cooley-Tukey with radix 16: each radix-16 DFT stage is written as a 16x16 complex matrix product against the DFT matrix, split into four real FP16 WMMA mma_sync calls (real/imag parts) on tensor cores. Several radix-16 stages plus a final radix-2 or radix-4 step are fused into one kernel (256-, 512- or 1024-point 'mergings') that keeps data in shared memory, so a 2^27-point transform needs only three global-memory passes. Twiddle multiplication and the small radix-2/4 tails run as ordinary half2 CUDA-core arithmetic.
when_to_use: Large batches of forward FP16 complex FFTs whose size is exactly one of the hard-coded lengths (for example 1M batches of 256/512/1024 points) on a V100 or A100.
Throughput-bound pipelines that already tolerate FP16 error (mixed-precision ML or signal pre-processing) and can produce input in the library's digit-reversed order for free.
As a reference design if you are writing your own tensor-core FFT kernels; the code is about 2,600 lines of CUDA in two files.
Reproducing or extending the CLUSTER 2021 tcFFT paper's experiments.
when_not_to_use: Anything needing accuracy: it accumulates in FP16 (half accumulator fragments), and open issue #5 reports a mean relative error of 1.9 for tcFFT versus 0.0185 for cuFFT FP16 on an RTX 3090 with the repo's own accuracy test; issue #2 reports NaN output after tcfftExec.

Any size not in the switch table, inverse transforms, real-to-complex, 3D, FP32/FP64 or non-power-of-two lengths: none exist (issue #1 asked for sizes beyond 1k; the inverse is requested in #2 and unanswered).
Production code: four commits in May 2021, no error checking on CUDA calls, no plan destructor (device twiddle buffers leak), five open/closed bug reports with no maintainer replies.
Closed-source or permissively licensed products: the code is GPL-3.0.
Non-NVIDIA GPUs or GPUs older than Volta: the Makefile builds sm_70 and sm_80 only and the kernels use nvcuda::wmma.

integration.dependencies: CUDA >= 11.0 runtime (cuda_fp16/mma.h); the header also includes cublas_v2.h; FFTW >= 3.3.8, cuFFT and OpenMP only for the test/benchmark binaries
integration.min_toolchain: nvcc from CUDA 11.0+, -std=c++11; host compiler with OpenMP for the harness
integration.platforms: NVIDIA tensor-core GPUs, Makefile targets sm_70 (V100) and sm_80 (A100); Linux Makefile only
integration.thread_safety: not documented; the plan is a plain struct passed by value and tcfftExec launches on the default stream with no stream parameter
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same job as cufftXtExec with CUDA_C_16F forward C2C, but a different API, fixed size table, and the input must be pre-permuted into digit-reversed order

gotchas: Unsupported sizes fall through 'default: break' in tcfftCreate, leaving n_radices/n_mergings uninitialized; tcfftExec then launches with garbage values. In 2D, Nx = 1024 selects plan.layer_1[2], a function pointer that tcfftCreate never sets.

The repo benchmark permutes the input into digit-reversed order on the host inside setup(), outside the timed loop, while cuFFT is timed on natural-order input; a real user has to pay for that permutation (an extra full read and write of the array) somewhere, so the published speedups are an upper bound.
The *_A100 kernel variants in tcfft_half.cu and tcfft_half_2d.cu are never bound by tcfftCreate (tcfftExec is commented '// V100'); how the paper's A100 runs selected them is not documented.

Small sizes launch N*batch/(n_cont*RADIX) blocks (n_cont = 32, 16, 8 for 256, 512, 1024), so batch counts that are not a multiple of 32/16/8 leave trailing transforms unprocessed; test.sh only says the batch 'should bigger than 32 for short sizes'.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick tcFFT over VkFFT or TurboFFT only for batched forward FP16 transforms at its exact sizes where tensor-core throughput matters more than accuracy; VkFFT (FP16/32/64, any size, inverse, Vulkan/CUDA/HIP/OpenCL, MIT) and TurboFFT (FP32/FP64, fault tolerance) are maintained, general libraries and the safer choice otherwise.
verified_claims_summary: The tcFFT paper (arXiv 2104.11471, IEEE CLUSTER 2021) reports average speedups of 1.29x-3.24x on V100 and 1.10x-3.03x on A100 over cuFFT 11.0 FP16 for batched 1D and 2D C2C FFTs; the repo's paired speed binaries time repeated in-place forward transforms with gettimeofday for at least 4 s per size, built by nvcc with -std=c++11 for sm_70/sm_80 and no explicit -O flag. The digit-reversal permutation is excluded from the tcFFT timing, and the host CPU and exact CUDA version are not stated in the repo.
status_note: Abandoned research code (four commits, May 2021, no maintainer replies to issues); GPL-3.0 and small enough to vendor, but treat it as a reference implementation rather than a library.
